subject: Mutual acceptance protocol & edge-case validation plan
body:
From: Evan Ross <evan.ross@brightbridgehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightbridgehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Acceptance gates & edge-case validation plan

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput numbers looked promising. As we start scoping the evaluation, BD and engineering here want a concise acceptance protocol we can use during a 2-week pilot. High-level asks from my side:

- Clear pass/fail thresholds for latency (95th %-ile) and inference cost per 1K requests.
- A short list of representative edge cases (P0/P1) so we can surface failure modes.
- Evidence we can provide for our compliance reviewers (audit log access, SOC2 artifacts).
- A mutual action plan (MAP) with owners and checkpoints so legal/procurement know when they need to move.

Can you send a draft MAP and an acceptance test catalog? If possible, include an ‘escape hatch’ — a list of conditions where we stop the pilot and fall back to the prior service (we have strict patient-data SLAs).

Attaching a short requirements doc from our side: BBH-eval-requirements.pdf

If you prefer, we can do a 30-min working session next week to walk through the MAP.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Ross
Director, Partnerships — BrightBridge Health

---

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Evan Ross <evan.ross@brightbridgehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance gates & edge-case validation plan

Hi Evan —

Appreciate the clarity. I’ve put together a proposed MAP + acceptance checklist (attached) that maps tests to owners and acceptance signals. Summary below — full details are in MAP_BBH_v1.xlsx.

High-level success criteria (pass = all three):
1) Latency: 95th %-ile <= 420ms for 1–4k tokens (measured at our edge).
2) Accuracy/concordance: task-specific F1 >= 0.86 on our curated sample set (we’ll share vectors).
3) Cost/capacity: average per-inference token cost <= your target X (we list options) and no sustained throttling under 80% of expected throughput.

Exit gates (stop the pilot if any triggered):
- Data leakage event or lack of audit logs within 24 hours of request.
- Repeated rate-limiting that causes >5% user-visible errors in a 24h window.
- Model behavior in top 10 P0 edge cases produces unsafe outputs after two mitigation attempts.

Acceptance tests we propose (short):
- Smoke test: end-to-end generation with seeded prompts, verify latency, token counts, and basic correctness (owner: Redwood SE — ben_carter).
- Concordance run: run curated 500-case set, compute F1 and false positives (owner: BrightBridge clinical QA — Priya Shah).
- Stress run: synthetic traffic ramp to planned throughput (owner: Redwood infra — karthik_iyer).
- Observability check: access to per-request token logs, latency histograms, and tracing for any failure (owner: Redwood ops).

Compliance/ evidence: we will provide SOC2 summary and a short audit log export for the pilot window. For anything requiring KMS or HSM proof, we’ll coordinate with your security contacts and can provide redacted artifacts.

Attachments: MAP_BBH_v1.xlsx (MAP + owners + timeline) and a zip of the acceptance test vectors (acceptance-test-vectors.zip). I added a 5-day mid-pilot checkpoint to decide go/no-go.

Next steps: can you confirm (a) you have the vectors/priorities (b) pilot start date preference (we suggested Oct 20) and (c) legal/procurement timeline for signature? I’ll queue the DocuSign link after we align.

Thanks — looping in Karthik + Ben for SLA and throughput items.

—
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0218

On Fri, Oct 10, 2025 at 13:47, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> Thanks Marissa and Evan — quick note on the stress / throughput acceptance so we’re aligned:
>
> - Stress run target: 1.2x expected steady-state QPS for 30 minutes, then back to steady state for 60 minutes. Failure if sustained token backlog or p99 latency > 900ms for more than 10 minutes.
> - Fallback plan: if the production variant exceeds p99 target, we’ll automatically route to a compatible lighter quantized variant with documented quality delta.
> - Test ownership: I’ll own the stress run and provide the runbook + Grafana dashboard link before the pilot.
>
> Link to shared test vectors and runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cBBH-eval-tests
>
> Ben — please confirm you can own smoke/concordance validation and the sample artifacts.
>
> Karthik
> VP, Product — Redwood Inference
>

From: Evan Ross <evan.ross@brightbridgehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightbridgehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance gates & edge-case validation plan

Marissa — this is great, thanks to you and the team. We reviewed the MAP and acceptance tests with BD and security this morning. Quick responses:

- We can provide the curated 500-case vector set by EOD Friday (Priya to own).
- The SOC2 summary and audit log samples are acceptable for the pilot; our security team will request a Redacted KMS configuration later if pilot proceeds.
- Pilot start: Oct 21 works for us; we accept the 5-day mid-pilot checkpoint on Oct 26 (we’ll lock a 30-min decision slot).
- Escape hatch: agreed — if any exit gate is triggered we pause and re-evaluate; please add a short amendment to the MAP describing the pause workflow for procurement.

Please send the DocuSign when ready and Ben/Karthik let us know runbook availability so we can schedule the stress run window.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Evan
Director, Partnerships — BrightBridge Health

[DocuSign placeholder will be posted to HubSpot when MAP is finalized]
